newsitem.title: USA: Unocal closes downstream deal with PdVSA.
newsitem.headline: Unocal closes downstream deal with PdVSA.

text.p: A unit of Venezuelan state oil concern Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA) said Thursday that it had formally closed a deal for the purchase of Unocal Corp's downstream assets in the U.S. MidWest.
PdVSA unit CITGO Petroleum Corp will operate the assets acquired by PDV Midwest Refining for $250 million.
The deal was originally announced in December.

The assets include a 153,000 barrels per day (bpd) refinery near Chicago, Illinois, which has a relationship network with some 200 wholesalers and supplies 2,300 independently-owned "76" branded retail outlets across 15 states in the Midwest and Eastern U.S.
PdVSA will also acquire a lubricants belnding plant in Cincinnati, Ohio and storage terminals across the 15-state region covered.
The refinery will run Venezuelan crude oil shipped up to the U.S. Gulf and transferred by pipeline.
The assets were previously held by UNO-VEN, a 50-50 joint venture between PdVSA and Unocal.
"Strategically, the UNO-VEN assets fall in a region which represents a major element of CITGO's long-term expansion plans," said Ralph Cunningham, CITGO president and chief executive.

"Although CITGO has had a presence in the Midwest for some time, there were considerable logistical barriers to significant expansion. Our operating the UNO-VEN assets togther with our Eagle Pipeline which runs from the Gulf Coast to Drumright, Oklahoma, means that most of those barriers have been removed. Among other considerations, we believe that growing our business in such important regions as the Midwest and Ohio Valley will substantially enhance our brand value," Cunningham said.
